Founding Full-Stack AI Engineer — Interview Transcript

Interviewer: Tell me about yourself and your experience building AI products.

Candidate: Hi, I'm Amit Kumar. I recently completed my B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering from IIIT Sri City. My main focus is full-stack development and AI engineering. I've built applications using Python, FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Docker. Some of my key projects include InterviewLens, a multi-agent interview evaluation platform, and RAG-GPT, a document question-answering application with hybrid retrieval and automated evaluation. I also worked as an AI/ML Research Intern at DRDO, where I benchmarked object detection models on accuracy, latency, and model size.

Interviewer: Tell me about InterviewLens. What problem does it solve?

Candidate: InterviewLens addresses the problem of unreliable interview feedback. I built a full-stack application using React, FastAPI, MongoDB Atlas, and LLM APIs. It uses five asynchronous multi-agent stages to evaluate interview responses. One of its key components is a Verification Agent that checks whether generated feedback is grounded in transcript timestamps. I also implemented persistent cross-session state with user-isolated data scoping. In my evaluation, the multi-agent workflow scored 9.4 out of 10 on output quality, compared with 3.2 out of 10 for a single-step baseline.

Interviewer: Why did you choose a multi-agent architecture instead of a single LLM call?

Candidate: I chose a multi-agent architecture because different stages have different responsibilities, such as analyzing an answer, identifying weaknesses, and verifying evidence. Separating these responsibilities makes the workflow easier to evaluate and debug. However, I wouldn't use multiple agents for every task because they increase latency and cost. I'd compare the multi-agent workflow against a simpler baseline and retain the additional complexity only when it provides measurable improvements.

Interviewer: Explain the architecture of your RAG-GPT project.

Candidate: RAG-GPT is a document question-answering application deployed on AWS EC2 using Docker. It supports PDF ingestion, OCR-enabled extraction, and overlapping text chunking. For retrieval, I combine semantic search using ChromaDB with BM25 keyword search. I fuse the rankings using Reciprocal Rank Fusion and then apply cross-encoder reranking before passing the selected context to the LLM. I also implemented Ragas-based evaluation, hallucination checks, PostgreSQL session memory, and TTL-based response caching.

Interviewer: How do you evaluate the quality of an AI-generated answer?

Candidate: I look at both retrieval quality and answer quality. For retrieval, I consider whether the system retrieves relevant context. For generated answers, I evaluate relevance and faithfulness to the available evidence. In RAG-GPT, I used Ragas metrics, including faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall. I'd also maintain a representative evaluation dataset and run regression tests whenever I change the model, prompt, or retrieval pipeline.

Interviewer: Describe a backend optimization you implemented.

Candidate: In Meal-Monkey, my food delivery application, I optimized API performance using Redis caching, database indexing, and pagination. In my load tests, mean API latency decreased from 83.7 milliseconds to 6 milliseconds, approximately a 14-times improvement. The p95 latency decreased from 232.8 milliseconds to 7.9 milliseconds. The test covered 300 requests with zero reported errors. I would also monitor cache hit rates and implement appropriate invalidation strategies to prevent stale data.

Interviewer: Suppose your AI application suddenly starts producing incorrect answers. How would you debug it?

Candidate: I'd first identify whether the issue is in retrieval, prompt construction, model generation, or post-processing. I'd inspect representative failed requests and compare the retrieved context with the expected evidence. If retrieval is poor, I'd investigate chunking, embeddings, ranking, and reranking. If the context is correct but the answer is wrong, I'd examine the prompt, model behavior, and output validation. I'd reproduce the failure, add a regression test, and deploy a fix after verifying it against the evaluation dataset.

Interviewer: How do you approach building a new feature from scratch?

Candidate: I start by understanding the user problem and defining measurable acceptance criteria. Then I identify the simplest architecture that can solve it, implement the API and data model, build the frontend, and integrate any AI components. I test normal cases, edge cases, authentication, and failure handling before deployment. After shipping, I monitor errors, latency, usage, and cost. I prefer shipping a small, reliable version early and improving it based on actual feedback.

Interviewer: How do you use AI coding tools in your development workflow?

Candidate: I use Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot to accelerate prototyping and repetitive coding tasks. I don't blindly trust generated code. I review it for correctness, security, maintainability, and performance, then run tests and inspect critical execution paths. I break larger tasks into smaller changes with clear acceptance criteria. AI tools help me move faster, but I remain responsible for the quality of the code I ship.

Interviewer: Why do you want to join as a founding full-stack engineer?

Candidate: I'm interested in roles where I can take ownership of a product end to end. My experience spans frontend development, backend engineering, databases, deployment, AI integration, and evaluation. I enjoy solving ambiguous problems, making practical architectural decisions, and measuring whether a solution actually works. As a founding engineer, I'd like to contribute not only by writing code but also by helping shape the product, identifying technical trade-offs, and building reliable systems that can scale with user needs.

Interviewer: Do you have any questions for us?

Candidate: Yes. What is the biggest engineering challenge the team is currently facing, and what would you expect the founding full-stack engineer to accomplish in the first 30 days?

segments.text: Founding Full-Stack AI Engineer — Interview Transcript

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Tell me about yourself and your experience building AI products.

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: Hi, I'm Amit Kumar. I recently completed my B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering from IIIT Sri City. My main focus is full-stack development and AI engineering. I've built applications using Python, FastAPI, React, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Docker. Some of my key projects include InterviewLens, a multi-agent interview evaluation platform, and RAG-GPT, a document question-answering application with hybrid retrieval and automated evaluation. I also worked as an AI/ML Research Intern at DRDO, where I benchmarked object detection models on accuracy, latency, and model size.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Tell me about InterviewLens. What problem does it solve?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: InterviewLens addresses the problem of unreliable interview feedback. I built a full-stack application using React, FastAPI, MongoDB Atlas, and LLM APIs. It uses five asynchronous multi-agent stages to evaluate interview responses. One of its key components is a Verification Agent that checks whether generated feedback is grounded in transcript timestamps. I also implemented persistent cross-session state with user-isolated data scoping. In my evaluation, the multi-agent workflow scored 9.4 out of 10 on output quality, compared with 3.2 out of 10 for a single-step baseline.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Why did you choose a multi-agent architecture instead of a single LLM call?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: I chose a multi-agent architecture because different stages have different responsibilities, such as analyzing an answer, identifying weaknesses, and verifying evidence. Separating these responsibilities makes the workflow easier to evaluate and debug. However, I wouldn't use multiple agents for every task because they increase latency and cost. I'd compare the multi-agent workflow against a simpler baseline and retain the additional complexity only when it provides measurable improvements.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Explain the architecture of your RAG-GPT project.

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: RAG-GPT is a document question-answering application deployed on AWS EC2 using Docker. It supports PDF ingestion, OCR-enabled extraction, and overlapping text chunking. For retrieval, I combine semantic search using ChromaDB with BM25 keyword search. I fuse the rankings using Reciprocal Rank Fusion and then apply cross-encoder reranking before passing the selected context to the LLM. I also implemented Ragas-based evaluation, hallucination checks, PostgreSQL session memory, and TTL-based response caching.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: How do you evaluate the quality of an AI-generated answer?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: I look at both retrieval quality and answer quality. For retrieval, I consider whether the system retrieves relevant context. For generated answers, I evaluate relevance and faithfulness to the available evidence. In RAG-GPT, I used Ragas metrics, including faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall. I'd also maintain a representative evaluation dataset and run regression tests whenever I change the model, prompt, or retrieval pipeline.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Describe a backend optimization you implemented.

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: In Meal-Monkey, my food delivery application, I optimized API performance using Redis caching, database indexing, and pagination. In my load tests, mean API latency decreased from 83.7 milliseconds to 6 milliseconds, approximately a 14-times improvement. The p95 latency decreased from 232.8 milliseconds to 7.9 milliseconds. The test covered 300 requests with zero reported errors. I would also monitor cache hit rates and implement appropriate invalidation strategies to prevent stale data.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Suppose your AI application suddenly starts producing incorrect answers. How would you debug it?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: I'd first identify whether the issue is in retrieval, prompt construction, model generation, or post-processing. I'd inspect representative failed requests and compare the retrieved context with the expected evidence. If retrieval is poor, I'd investigate chunking, embeddings, ranking, and reranking. If the context is correct but the answer is wrong, I'd examine the prompt, model behavior, and output validation. I'd reproduce the failure, add a regression test, and deploy a fix after verifying it against the evaluation dataset.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: How do you approach building a new feature from scratch?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: I start by understanding the user problem and defining measurable acceptance criteria. Then I identify the simplest architecture that can solve it, implement the API and data model, build the frontend, and integrate any AI components. I test normal cases, edge cases, authentication, and failure handling before deployment. After shipping, I monitor errors, latency, usage, and cost. I prefer shipping a small, reliable version early and improving it based on actual feedback.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: How do you use AI coding tools in your development workflow?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: I use Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot to accelerate prototyping and repetitive coding tasks. I don't blindly trust generated code. I review it for correctness, security, maintainability, and performance, then run tests and inspect critical execution paths. I break larger tasks into smaller changes with clear acceptance criteria. AI tools help me move faster, but I remain responsible for the quality of the code I ship.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Why do you want to join as a founding full-stack engineer?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: I'm interested in roles where I can take ownership of a product end to end. My experience spans frontend development, backend engineering, databases, deployment, AI integration, and evaluation. I enjoy solving ambiguous problems, making practical architectural decisions, and measuring whether a solution actually works. As a founding engineer, I'd like to contribute not only by writing code but also by helping shape the product, identifying technical trade-offs, and building reliable systems that can scale with user needs.

segments.text: Do you have any questions for us?

segments.speaker: candidate
segments.text: Yes. What is the biggest engineering challenge the team is currently facing, and what would you expect the founding full-stack engineer to accomplish in the first 30 days?
